# T3.06-T3.09: rate control, low latency, slices

The reference client is no help for rate control: it fills the RC structure (2 Mbit/s, 4 Mbit CPB, GOP 250) but runs
`RCMODE` 0 (constant QP), which is why it ignores the bitrate. What it does show is how the fields are encoded:
`Ravg` = `R` = bits per pixel per frame in 23.8 fixed point (2 000 000 / 25 / (256x128) x 256 = 625, as captured),
`framerate` = fps x 256, `maxQPD` 6, `baseQPD` 3.

`EncConfig` got `rc_mode` (the `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS` RCMODE value), `bitrate`, `max_bitrate`, `vbv_bits`, `fps`,
`slices`. The RC fields are filled as above (hrd_type 2, buffersize = nal/vcl CPB = `vbv_bits`, nal/vcl bitrate =
`max_bitrate`, gop_length and Np from `idr_period`). `SET_IO_RC_PROCESS` (persistent RC state, zeroed at open) and
`SET_IN_RCDATA` are always sent.

Content: `encodeN` 1920x1080, 120 frames, 1 ref; at constant QP 28 it costs ~12 Mbit/s. "Steady" = frames 10..119.

## T3.06 CBR

| mode | target | steady rate | largest P | avgQP | luma |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 (picture CBR) | 8 Mbit/s | 8.35 | 197.5 kbit | 28..37 | 40.6 dB |
| 18 (MB-row CBR) | 8 Mbit/s | 8.32 | 200.3 kbit | 28..37 | 40.6 dB |
| 2 | 20 Mbit/s | 19.89 | 395.3 kbit | 16..18 | 51.9 dB |
| 18 | 20 Mbit/s | 19.98 | 405.9 kbit | 17..18 | 52.0 dB |
| 2 | 40 Mbit/s | 39.40 | 786.6 kbit | 9..11 | 54.5 dB |
| 18 | 40 Mbit/s | 39.74 | 792.6 kbit | 9..11 | 54.5 dB |

Within ±5 % of the target. A target below what QP 51 can reach (5 Mbit/s for this content) ends at QP 50 and 7.4
Mbit/s, as it should.

## T3.07 VBR

| mode | target / max | steady rate | largest P (as rate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (picture VBR) | 10 / 20 Mbit/s | 11.30 | 266 kbit (16 Mbit/s) |
| 17 (MB-row VBR) | 10 / 20 Mbit/s | 12.01 | 254 kbit (15 Mbit/s) |
| 1 | 20 / 40 Mbit/s | 22.68 | 472 kbit (28 Mbit/s) |

Average 13-20 % above target, peaks well under max. Usable; not tuned.

## T3.08 low latency

One-frame VBV (`vbv_bits` = bitrate / fps), MB-row CBR, 20 Mbit/s at 60 fps (333 kbit per frame), IDR every 30:

- no frame exceeds the budget: largest P 323 kbit, **IDRs 315-351 kbit** (the RC raises their QP to 33-34), steady
  16.5 Mbit/s (the RC stays a little under with a one-frame buffer; with a 2-frame VBV it is 20.05 Mbit/s);
- all 70 frames decode, 48.0 dB average, 34 dB on the IDRs.
- **`single_frame_VBV` must stay 0**: set to 1 with the same settings the rate went to 60 Mbit/s at QP 5-6. It's
  left 0 in `enc.c`.

No B-frames, infinite GOP unless `idr_period`, IDR on request with `enc_encode(force_idr)`.

## T3.09 slices

- **`slice_mode` 0 + one slice control per slice works** (`num_forced_slices_minus1` = n-1, whole MB rows spread
  evenly): 3, 4, 8 and 16 slices per frame, every picture decodes (1080p, 2 refs: 46.9-47.1 dB at constant QP; with
  CBR the per-frame budget still holds). `slice_mode` 1 hangs the engine here too (with 4 controls, with or without
  `SLICE_STAT_ON` + stat offsets), so nvenc_drv.h's description of the two modes doesn't match what Ada does.
- Size-limited slices (`max_slice_size`) have no effect in `slice_mode` 0 so far. Not needed for M3; maybe later for
  streaming (with `SUBFRAME_MODE`).
- An earlier split (`ceil(rows / n)` per slice) gave the last slice a negative MB count at 16 slices / 68 rows; the
  engine then produced 14 slices. Rows are now spread evenly.
